h: Team tactics and the rest of the city
p: Every escape room crew has its characters. There's the organiser who reads every note twice, the searcher who's under the table before the door's even shut, and the one who quietly cracks the final code while everyone else is arguing. The best results come when you let everyone play to their strengths and keep talking. Call out what you've found, put used items to one side so you don't keep revisiting them, and don't be shy about asking your host for a nudge.

If you're a bigger group, consider splitting into two rooms. Racing your mates in the room next door, then comparing times over food afterwards, turns a simple outing into a proper event. Just make sure everyone agrees on the stakes beforehand, whether that's buying the first round or picking the restaurant.

Cabot Circus is well placed for exploring the older side of Bristol too. A short walk west takes you to Castle Park, where the bombed-out shell of St Peter's Church stands as a memorial among the gardens by the water. Keep going and you'll reach St Nicholas Market, a historic covered market packed with food stalls and independent traders, which is a brilliant place for lunch. King Street, home to the Bristol Old Vic theatre and a row of characterful old pubs, is close by as well, and the quirky stepped lane of Christmas Steps is worth a wander for its little shops. Temple Meads station is around a quarter of an hour away on foot, so it's easy enough to arrive by train and leave the car at home.
